title: Labour Force Survey quality update: April 2026
date_evidence: Release date: 21 April 2026 ... Office for National Statistics (ONS), released 21 April 2026, ONS website, article, Labour Force Survey quality update: April 2026
key_claim: UK Labour Force Survey statistics remain badged 'official statistics in development'; there were 77,927 responses in Oct-Dec 2025, up 33,689 from the Jul-Sep 2023 low but still 6,135 below Oct-Dec 2019; the ONS recommends using LFS estimates alongside PAYE RTI and Claimant Count, and aims to transition headline statistics to the Transformed Labour Force Survey in 2027.
notes: Tier 1 national statistics office. Primary anchor for the UK labour-data reliability story: response recovery, residual caution, 'official statistics in development' status, TLFS 2027 transition.

title: More than Missing Data: Survey Response Rates Following the 2025 Government Shutdown
date_evidence: meta-afo_contentDate: 2026-04-09T10:00:00Z ... # More than Missing Data: Survey Response Rates Following the 2025 Government Shutdown April 09, 2026
key_claim: The US Current Population Survey response rate fell from 90% in 2013 to 82% by February 2020 and below 70% by 2024; the October 2025 CPS was cancelled during the government shutdown and the post-shutdown response rate fell almost 5 percentage points from September to November, with newly enrolled households responding persistently below trend, which if sustained will diminish confidence in monthly unemployment statistics.
notes: Tier 1 central-bank research. US anchor: long-run CPS response-rate decline plus the shutdown shock and its lingering compositional effect.

title: Long-term international migration, provisional: year ending December 2025
date_evidence: # Long-term international migration, provisional: year ending December 2025 ... Official statistics in development. ... Release date: 21 May 2026
key_claim: Provisional UK long-term net migration was 171,000 in the year ending December 2025, down from the updated 331,000 a year earlier; total long-term immigration was 813,000, down 20% from the updated 1,012,000; the bulletin is badged 'official statistics in development'.
notes: Tier 1 national statistics office. Latest provisional migration figures, illustrating both the headline fall and the 'in development' status and revision behaviour.

title: International migration research, progress update: April 2026
date_evidence: # International migration research, progress update: April 2026 ... Release date: 23 April 2026 ... This marked a major milestone for us with LTIM no longer using any International Passenger Survey (IPS) data ... They are now based on observed behaviours within admin data.
key_claim: From the November 2025 publication, ONS long-term international migration estimates no longer use any International Passenger Survey data and are based instead on administrative data (Home Office Borders and Immigration data and the DWP RAPID database); multiple migrant groups (overstayers, ILR holders, temporary mobility) are still at proof-of-concept or development stage.
verbatim_quote: This marked a major milestone for us with LTIM no longer using any International Passenger Survey (IPS) data.
notes: Tier 1 national statistics office. Anchor for the structural pivot from survey to administrative data in migration measurement.

title: Making sense of labor market indicators amid data imperfections (BPEA Spring 2026)
date_evidence: BPEA | Spring 2026 # Making sense of labor market indicators amid data imperfections ... March 25, 2026 ... their framework ... can fill in the gaps when government reports are delayed, such as during the federal government shutdown last fall.
key_claim: A Brookings Papers on Economic Activity study by Federal Reserve and academic economists builds a method aggregating 94 noisy and often conflicting labour-market indicators into estimated narratives (labour demand, supply, matching frictions); the framework can fill gaps when official reports are delayed, as during the autumn 2025 federal shutdown, because missing observations in individual series do not prevent estimation.
notes: Tier 2 think-tank / peer-style conference paper. Evidence that the analytical community is building composite, gap-filling methods in response to degraded and delayed official data.

title: Net migration to the UK
date_evidence: # Net migration to the UK 18 Dec 2025 ... ONS has revised the estimate of net migration for 2024 downwards by 20%, or 86,000, since it was first published. ... administrative data ... have the potential to improve migration statistics, but are not yet labelled National Statistics as they have important limitations.
key_claim: ONS revised its 2024 net migration estimate down by 86,000 (20%) after first publication; new administrative-data methods have the potential to improve migration statistics but are not yet National Statistics and have important limitations; official net-migration projections have usually undershot future levels over the past 20 years.
notes: Structural anchor (18 Dec 2025, ~5.5 months). Canonical independent briefing on UK net migration; used for the persistent-revision and admin-data-limitation points and for the counter-argument.

title: Why the crisis in official statistics matters - and how it can be fixed (Editorial)
date_evidence: meta-dc.date: 2026-03-17 ... EDITORIAL 17 March 2026 # Why the crisis in official statistics matters - and how it can be fixed ... a crisis affecting official statistics that has been triggered by three main factors: inadequate funding, political overreach and plummeting response rates.
key_claim: A Nature editorial, drawing on interviews with more than 20 researchers and national-statistics staff worldwide, frames a global crisis in official statistics triggered by three factors - inadequate funding, political overreach and plummeting survey response rates - and notes the IMF publicly assesses countries whose data collection falls short.
notes: Tier 3 quality scientific journalism (editorial). Globalises the signal beyond the UK/US and names the three structural drivers.
